editorial:
If you want a loud, silly comedy built around one actor playing several wild characters, this movie throws you right into the chaos. You follow Norbit, a sweet but timid guy who gets pushed around by Rasputia, his loud and controlling fiancée, while he quietly reconnects with Kate, the kind woman he loved as a kid. The whole thing feels like a cartoon brought to life, with big jokes, bigger personalities, and plenty of awkward situations. It is not subtle, and it leans hard on physical comedy and outrageous behavior, so you should know what you are getting before you press play.

The standout part is Eddie Murphy’s energy as he jumps between roles, especially the over-the-top Rasputia, and the movie moves quickly from one gag to the next. The downside is that many jokes feel mean-spirited or repetitive, and the story is pretty thin once the setup is clear. If you enjoy broad, silly humor and do not mind crude jokes, you might get a few laughs. If you prefer smart comedy, skip it. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Norbit finally stands up to Rasputia and her brothers, stopping their plan to take over Kate’s orphanage and force her into a bad marriage. Kate realizes Norbit is the boy from her past and chooses him instead. Rasputia and her family are humiliated and driven away, while Norbit and Kate get married and celebrate with the kids from the orphanage. The twist is that Norbit’s gentle nature wins out, and the movie ends with him finally free from Rasputia’s control.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves broad physical comedy and outrageous characters.
